topic: Megawatt Watch 27-28 Oct: Crusoe Paraguay, ARC x Compal MOU, STT GDC Tokyo, CoreWeave Denmark, SoleCrypt Tunisia

sources.title: Crusoe and Araico to build 280 MW AI data center near Paraguay's Itaipú Dam
facts: Crusoe and Araico will build AI compute next to the Itaipú substation in Paraguay, powered by the Itaipú hydroelectric dam
Initial deployment slated to come online in mid-2027
Path to 106 MW of IT capacity; options to expand to approximately 280 MW
Crusoe's first AI cloud deployment in Latin America; serves US and Latin American customers via Crusoe Cloud

sources.title: ARC Cloud and Compal sign MOU eyeing 100 MW of AI data center capacity
facts: ARC Cloud (Accelerated Research Computing) and Compal Electronics signed an MOU at the 2026 OCP Global Summit
They will explore opportunities related to a data center development roadmap of up to 100 MW
No financial terms, timeline or committed capacity disclosed; ARC Cloud plans AI infrastructure investment across the United States

sources.title: CoreWeave deploys AI infrastructure in Denmark
facts: CoreWeave's first Denmark deployment, with atNorth, hosts 22.5 MW of IT capacity at the DEN01 data center in Copenhagen
Scheduled to go live in Q4 2026; NVIDIA Blackwell systems with Quantum-X800 InfiniBand
CoreWeave will supply surplus heat to Copenhagen's district heating network
CoreWeave Europe: 9 data centers across 5 countries

sources.title: STTGDC secures US$ 590 million green loan for expansion of Tokyo DC campus
facts: STT GDC secured a US$590 million green loan to fit out and operate STTGDC TYO1 and TYO2, Goodman Business Park, Inzai City, Greater Tokyo
The campus will provide a combined 70.8 MW of IT capacity

sources.title: SoleCrypt ups size of planned data center campus in Bizerte, Tunisia
facts: Headline: SoleCrypt ups size of planned data center campus in Bizerte, Tunisia
Standfirst: first 7MW phase due live in early 2028, to host Vera Rubin GPUs

caption:
480 MW of new data center capacity was announced in two days, across five projects.

The biggest number, 280 MW next to Paraguay's Itaipú dam, is a long-term option; the first phases have a path to 106 MW of IT capacity. The 100 MW from ARC Cloud and Compal is an MOU. The firmest builds are smaller: 70.8 MW in Tokyo and 22.5 MW in Copenhagen.

Headline megawatts are not all equal, so we label options and MOUs.

Data: Coloprice pipeline tracker, 28 Oct 2026. Sources: W.Media (27–28 Oct), DCD (27 Oct). Full list on the last slide.
